# How to Relearn DSA from Zero

**Source:** https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdecbsEnSGo/ · **Type:** Reel · **Author:** level5esper · **Saved:** 2026-10-05

**Why I saved it:** DSA

## Summary

This video outlines a strategy for mastering Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) that focuses on problem recognition and reasoning rather than relying on curated LeetCode or NeetCode lists. It recommends using the USACO Guide to build core algorithmic tools and AtCoder for granular, untagged practice.

## Transcript and on-screen text

Maguri here. If I had to relearn DSA from zero, this is how I would do it. I would use two resources that very few people talk about. Let me explain. LeetCode and NeetCode are popular because they're convenient, but I wouldn't use either as my main way to learn. Easy, Medium, and Hard are coarse labels, so it's hard to track your actual level, and a roadmap tells you the topic before you have to recognize it. That ecosystem compounds the problem: repetitive questions with little transferable reasoning, AI-generated editorials written for engagement, and beginners teaching other beginners bad habits. Start with the USACO Guide. Bronze and core Silver teach reusable tools and techniques: prefix sums, binary search, two pointers, sorting, graph traversal, and why each one works. After each topic, close the guide and solve a few sample problems under that topic. Then gradually introduce untagged problems, and record the observation you missed, because that is what transfers. Then use AtCoder for randomized practice. Its granular difficulty estimates keep you near the boundary where the problems are difficult enough to teach you, but still solvable. You might be thinking, 'I only want to pass interviews. Why are you sending me to competitive programming sites?' Because interviews test whether you can solve unseen problems. USACO teaches the core ideas, and AtCoder tests whether you can apply them without being told the topic. A roadmap only lists the topics. Use it as your entire curriculum, and you miss the depth that makes those ideas transferable. Send this to a friend who swears by NeetCode 150, and follow me if you want to get cracked at DSA.

## Caption

If I had to relearn DSA from zero, this is how I'd do it. (NOT NeetCode 150).

Every influencer out there only talks about "sheets", "roadmaps", "youtube videos". None of them actually compared all the platforms out there, and it does not teach the depth you need to solve unseen problems.

I've tried over 20+ platforms and I'll tell you exactly the best ones, and why.

I’d use the USACO Guide to build the tools, then AtCoder to calibrate difficulty. Start with tagged examples. Gradually remove the tags. That trains the part interviews actually test: solving a problem you haven’t already classified.
